initial_build_notes.text:
Implementation contract (short):

- Requirement -> owning files:
  - All active requirements (0-21) implemented by game/tetris_game.py; game/__init__.py is an empty package initializer.
- State ownership and interfaces:
  - Game state owned by TetrisGame class in game/tetris_game.py:
    - Attributes: cols:int, rows:int, grid:List[List[Optional[Tuple[int,int,int]]]], score:int, current_piece:dict or None, game_over:bool, fall_timer:float.
    - Methods:
      - spawn_piece() -> None
      - can_place(matrix:List[List[int]], x:int, y:int) -> bool
      - rotate_matrix(matrix:List[List[int]]) -> List[List[int]]
      - lock_piece() -> None
      - clear_lines() -> int (returns number cleared)
      - reset_game() -> None
  - Input -> action -> state -> feedback:
    - KEYDOWN Left/Right/Down/Up/R/Escape map to move/soft-drop/rotate/restart/quit.
    - If a control causes a state change it prints the exact message (MOVE LEFT, MOVE RIGHT, SOFT DROP, ROTATE, RESTART, QUIT) and flushes.
    - When score changes prints SCORE:<n>. When game ends prints GAME OVER.
  - Coordinate convention:
    - Grid coordinates: (x,column from 0..9, y,row from 0..19) with (0,0) top-left. Piece position (px,py) refers to top-left of its matrix within grid.
  - Lifecycle:
    - init: create empty grid, score 0, spawn first piece (or set game_over if spawn collides).
    - run: main loop updates fall timer, handles inputs, renders grid, current piece and HUD.
    - terminal: on game_over freeze spawning/locking; user may press R to reset.
    - reset: reset_game() clears grid, score, timers, sets game_over=False and spawns new piece.
    - quit: Escape or window close triggers QUIT print and exits.

I'll now write the promised files (game/__init__.py and game/tetris_game.py) and run a syntax check.

requirement_coverage.check: The game window title displays 'Simple Tetris'.
The game displays a grid with 10 columns and 20 rows.
Falling and locked blocks are rendered as solid colored squares, with each of the four piece shapes having a distinct color.
Only the square, line, L-shape, and T-shape pieces appear in the game.
After a piece locks or at game start, a new random piece appears at the top-middle of the grid.
A falling piece moves down one row automatically after a fixed time interval.
Pressing LEFT moves the falling piece one column to the left, if space allows. 'MOVE LEFT' is printed to console.
Pressing RIGHT moves the falling piece one column to the right, if space allows. 'MOVE RIGHT' is printed to console.
Pressing DOWN moves the falling piece one row down immediately, if space allows. 'SOFT DROP' is printed to console.
Attempting to move a piece left/right/down into a wall or locked block has no effect on the piece's position.
Pressing UP rotates the falling piece 90 degrees clockwise. 'ROTATE' is printed to console.
Attempting to rotate a piece into a wall or locked block has no effect on the piece's orientation.
When a falling piece reaches the bottom or lands on locked blocks, it becomes part of the locked blocks, and a new piece appears at the top-middle.
When a row is full of locked blocks, it disappears, all rows above it shift down, and the score increases by 100.
The current score is continuously displayed in the top-right corner of the game window.
If a newly spawned piece cannot be placed without overlapping locked blocks, the game ends.
Upon game over, 'GAME OVER' and the final score are displayed, and no new pieces appear. 'GAME OVER' is printed to console.
Pressing 'R' clears the grid, resets the score to 0, and starts a new game. 'RESTART' is printed to console.
Pressing 'Escape' closes the game window. 'QUIT' is printed to console.
The specified messages are printed to the console when the corresponding controls are successfully activated.
When the game ends, 'GAME OVER' is printed to the console.
The game produces no audio output.
